 Prime Video mystery thriller from creator of Netflix's The Gentleman is a 'must-watch'
 Ian Craig 2026년 10월 29일 목 오후 6:00 UTC 0 Hero Fiennes Tiffin, Natascha McElhone, and Donal Finn in Young Sherlock (Image: Daniel Smith/Prime) A compelling Prime Video series by the creator of Netflix smash The Gentleman has been hailed "an absolute gem". The complete first series of the programme is now available on the streaming platform, with a second already in production, so you could binge the whole thing in a weekend.
 Television expert Anubhuti Navin, who regularly showcases films and TV shows currently available to stream via her Instagram page The Watchlist Club, called the series a "must-watch". She said: "One of the finest series with zero boring episodes". The show premiered on Amazon Prime Video in March and rapidly established itself as a viewer favourite.
 Dónal Finn as James Moriarty, Zine Tseng as Xiao Wei, and Hero Fiennes Tiffin as Sherlock Holmes in Young Sherlock (Image: Daniel Smith/Prime) Young Sherlock charts the tale of a 19-year-old Sherlock Holmes, prior to his transformation into the globally celebrated master detective. Teaming up with associate James Moriarty, who subsequently becomes his greatest nemesis, Holmes becomes embroiled in a murder enquiry at Oxford University.
 It takes inspiration from a series of novels exploring Holmes' formative years written by Andy Lane, while also drawing upon Sir Arthur Conan Doyle's timeless tales. Starring Hero Fiennes Tiffin as the titular detective and Dónal Finn as Moriarty, the debut series also features Zine Tseng as Xiao Wei, Joseph Fiennes as Holmes' father Silas, and Colin Firth as Sir Bucephalus Hodge.
 The series was created by Guy Richie, mastermind behind Netflix hit The Gentleman and director of iconic gangster films Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels and Snatch. He also helmed two Sherlock Holmes movies in 2009 and 2011 starring Robert Downey Jr and Jude Law, and directed the opening two instalments of Young Sherlock, reports The Mirror .
 Filming took place at Llandaff Cathedral in Cardiff, along with locations in Monmouth, Bridgend, and at Margam Park near Port Talbot, as well as in Bristol and Spain. The debut season comprises eight episodes, with a second series greenlit in April. Game of Thrones actors Aidan Gillen and Indira Varma are joining the line-up, together with The Crown's Olivia Williams and Outlander's Sophie Skelton. The new series is expected to launch in 2027.
 The show boasts an 84 per cent critics' score on reviews aggregator Rotten Tomatoes , plus an 83 per cent audience rating. One viewer commented: "This was way more fun than I expected. A little over-the-top at times, but I liked the energy and the mystery kept me interested."
 Another reviewer noted: "With a talented cast, skilled direction, and intelligent writing, Young Sherlock is as compelling as it is intriguing. Every episode deepens your curiosity, not just about the mysteries, but about the journey of seeing how a young Sherlock Holmes evolves into the legendary detective."
 A further viewer commented: "Great chemistry between the lead actors with the pace, excitement and wit you'd can expect from Guy Ritchie. If you love Ritchie's stuff you'll love this."
 Not everyone was won over, however. One critic noted: "Not a terrible show, pretty straightforward mystery. However most of the episodes are shot so dark, and poorly, you can barely see what is happening on screen. It would probably be three stars if it were shot better."
